issues.legal_issue: A general statement in an official gazette about migration does not, without evidence connecting the particular family to that migration, establish that family’s migration for deciding its personal law.
material_facts: The defendants relied on an Indore State Gazette entry describing Dhangars generally as having migrated from the Mathura region to other areas.
The plaintiff’s family pleaded that it originally resided in Ahmednagar, and that assertion was not disputed.
There was no evidence that the plaintiff’s family or its ancestors had migrated from Mathura to Ahmednagar, or evidence connecting the family to the migrations described in the Gazette.
issues.conclusion: Statements in an official gazette about public or historical matters are relevant and may be given due consideration, but they are not conclusive on matters requiring judicial determination. The general Gazette entry did not establish that this family had migrated from Mathura.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 37 and 57(13) of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, statements in government gazettes and appropriate reference materials concerning public or historical matters are relevant; Section 81 permits a presumption of genuineness for gazettes coming from proper custody. Official statements may be valuable or corroborative evidence, but opinions or statements concerning private rights and matters requiring judicial adjudication are not conclusive. The Court relied on Rajah Muttu Ramalinga Setupati v. Perianayagum Pillai, Martand Rao v. Malhar Rao, Arunachellam Chetty v. Venkatachellapathi Guru Swamigal, Narayan Bhagwantrao Gosavi Balajiwale v. Gopal Vinayak Gosavi, The Poohari Fakir Sadavarthy of Bomdilipuram v. The Commissioner, Hindu Religious & Charitable Endowments, and Mahant Shri Srinivasa Ramanuj Das v. Surajnarayan Dass.

rule.if: family_property_succession_dispute and migration_from_an_origin_is_relied_on and only_general_gazette_migration_evidence and not evidence_connecting_family_to_migration

predicates.family_property_succession_dispute: A court is deciding a dispute over succession to family property.
predicates.migration_from_an_origin_is_relied_on: A party relies on the family having migrated from an asserted place of origin.
predicates.only_general_gazette_migration_evidence: The evidence consists only of a gazette statement about migration by a broader group, rather than evidence about the particular family.
predicates.evidence_connecting_family_to_migration: Evidence connects the particular family or its ancestors to the migration relied on.

issues.definition: When a family-property succession dispute depends on alleged migration, a general gazette account without evidence connecting the family to that migration does not establish that the family migrated from the asserted origin.

issues.legal_issue: A Hindu family that migrates carries its personal school of law with it unless the law of its origin is shown to have been renounced and the law of its new home adopted.
material_facts: The plaintiff’s family and the relevant ancestors were found to have been residents of Ahmednagar in the Bombay Province and later to have migrated to Indore.
The asserted earlier migration from Mathura was not proved.
The defendants did not establish that the family had renounced the law of its origin and adopted a different school of Hindu law in Indore.
issues.conclusion: The family carried to Indore the Mitakshara law of the Bombay school, rather than being governed by the Banaras school.
issues.legal_principle: A Hindu is governed by the personal branch of law carried from the place of origin. Where migration from one province to another is established, the presumption is that the migrant and descendants continue to be governed by the law or special custom of the former home; the party alleging renunciation and adoption of the new place’s law bears the onus. The Court relied on Balwant Rao v. Baji Rao, Keshao Rao Bapurao v. Sadasheorao Dajiba, and Udebhan Rajaram v. Vikram Ganu, as well as the stated principles in the cited Hindu law texts.

rule.if: family_property_succession_dispute and migration_from_origin_province_established and family_settled_in_new_province and not renunciation_of_origin_law_proved

predicates.family_property_succession_dispute: A court is deciding a dispute over succession to family property.
predicates.migration_from_origin_province_establish: The family’s migration from its earlier province of residence is established.
predicates.family_settled_in_new_province: The family moved from that province and settled in a different province.
predicates.renunciation_of_origin_law_proved: Evidence establishes that the family gave up the law of its origin and adopted the law of its new home.

issues.definition: In a family-property succession dispute, a family that migrated and settled elsewhere remains governed by its origin law when no renunciation of that law is proved.

issues.legal_issue: Under the Bombay school of Mitakshara law, a female bandhu within the applicable degree of relationship may inherit as a bandhu, and the stated list of bandhus is illustrative rather than exhaustive.
material_facts: The plaintiff was the deceased’s natural sister, but his adoption made her his father’s sister’s daughter and thus a bandhu through her mother’s side.
The plaintiff was found to be the deceased’s nearest bandhu within five degrees.
The family was governed by the Bombay school of Hindu law.
The deceased’s childless widow had held the estate as a limited owner and had gifted the disputed house; the plaintiff claimed succession to the estate after the widow’s death.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff was an heir to the deceased’s estate and entitled to possession of the disputed house with mesne profits; the gift did not defeat her entitlement.
issues.legal_principle: The Bombay school of Mitakshara law recognizes female bandhus as heirs, with nearness of blood applied to determine their order of succession; the enumeration of bandhus is illustrative, not exhaustive. The Court relied on Bhagirathibai v. Kahnujirav for the position of female heirs under Bombay law, and on Girdhari Lall Roy v. The Bengal Government and Muthuswami Mudaliyar v. Sunamedu Muthukumaraswami Mudaliyar for the non-exhaustive character of the enumeration. It also referred to the Mitakshara and the cited Hindu law texts concerning bandhus and succession.

rule.if: family_property_succession_dispute and bombay_mitakshara_law_applies and claimant_is_female_bandhu_within_five_degrees and claimant_is_nearest_eligible_bandhu

predicates.family_property_succession_dispute: A court is deciding a dispute over succession to family property.
predicates.bombay_mitakshara_law_applies: The family is governed by the Bombay school of Mitakshara law.
predicates.claimant_is_female_bandhu_within_five_de: The claimant is a female bandhu related to the deceased within five degrees.
predicates.claimant_is_nearest_eligible_bandhu: The claimant is the nearest eligible bandhu in the applicable order of succession.

issues.definition: A female bandhu inherits in a family-property succession dispute when Bombay Mitakshara law applies and she is the nearest eligible bandhu within five degrees.

issues.legal_issue: A mortgagee is not entitled to an equitable repayment decree against an heir when the mortgage money was not paid to that heir.
material_facts: The mortgagee sought repayment of money advanced to the donee who had mortgaged the house.
The money was not paid to the plaintiff, who succeeded to the estate.
The mortgagee’s claim against the mortgagor was not before the Court for final determination.
issues.conclusion: The mortgagee was not entitled to a repayment decree against the plaintiff, but could pursue any remedy available against the mortgagor.
issues.legal_principle: The Court rejected equitable repayment against the heir because the mortgage money had not been paid to the heir; it left the mortgagee free to pursue any remedy available against the mortgagor under law.

predicates.property_succession_dispute: A court is deciding a dispute concerning possession of property claimed through succession.
predicates.mortgagee_seeks_repayment_from_heir: A mortgagee asks the heir who claims the property to repay money advanced on the security of that property.
predicates.mortgage_money_not_paid_to_heir: The money advanced by the mortgagee was not paid to the heir from whom repayment is sought.

issues.definition: A mortgagee receives no repayment decree against an heir when the mortgagee seeks repayment from that heir but did not pay the mortgage money to the heir.
